_about: The voice-in spike's sheet (2026-10-23; design Rio 10-21/10-22, Andrew's amendments 10-21 and 10-23). TARGET rows: a `good` guide for the natural Coimbatore take and one or more `wrong` variants, each recorded; a variant's `label` is the ground truth the ear is judged against. Variants come from three sources, never invented to a quota: the charter (protocol/dialect.md: spoken forms, fusion, competent over local), her 07-31 ruling that natives mostly do not make the ல/ள and ர/ற distinctions (so a HARD trilled ற is wrong, the 'uncanny' sound), the nephew's 09-01 'book Tamil', and the English-mouth errors natives do hear (ழ as l, retroflex vs dental, vowel length, doubled consonants, the English th). TANGLISH rows: one natural take. FREE rows: Anna asks, he answers, then types what he meant. `ask` is the lesson moment the IN-CONTEXT ear is told about.

phrases.ask: Look outside and tell me what the weather is doing.
phrases.good: MA-zhai va-ru-dhu. The ழ: curl your tongue tip far back toward the roof of your mouth and let it hover without touching, a voiced glide like a deep American r. dhu: tongue tip soft on the back of your top teeth.

wrong.label: ழ said as an English l: malai (mountain)
wrong.how: Say MA-lai: tongue tip flat on the ridge behind your top teeth, an ordinary English l. Keep varudhu the same.

wrong.label: book form: varugiradhu
wrong.how: Say mazhai va-ru-gi-ra-dhu, the written verb, every syllable spelled out like a newsreader.

phrases.ask: Ask your aunt for a banana.
phrases.good: VAA-zhaip-pa-zham ku-dun-ga. Both ழ are the curled-back hover. Hold vaa long, and give the doubled pp a tiny stop. ku: an unaspirated k, no puff of air.

wrong.label: both ழ as English l: vaalaippalam
wrong.how: Say VAA-laip-pa-lam: both ழ become an English l. Leave the rest alone.

wrong.label: English aspirated k and d: khudunga
wrong.how: Say the English way: a puff of air on the k (hold your hand in front of your mouth and feel it) and an English d with the tip on the ridge: KHU-dun-ga.

phrases.ask: Tell me the kids are asleep.
phrases.good: ku-ZHAN-dhai-nga THOON-git-taan-ga. ழ is the curled-back hover. Hold thoo and taa long. The doubled ட்ட: curl the tongue tip back, touch the roof and hold it.

wrong.label: ழ as English l: kulandhainga
wrong.how: Say ku-LAN-dhai-nga with an English l. Keep the rest as in your best take.

wrong.label: book form: kuzhandhaigal thoongivittaargal
wrong.how: Say the written sentence: ku-zhan-dhai-gal thoon-gi-vit-taar-gal, the full plural and full verb, read like a book.

phrases.ask: Ask your niece to sing.
phrases.good: PAAT-tu PAA-dun-ga. ட்டு: curl your tongue tip back, hit the roof hard and hold for the double. Hold both paa long. The d in paadunga is that same curled spot, said softly.

wrong.label: dental tt: paaththu (look)
wrong.how: Say PAATH-thu: tongue tip on the back of your top teeth, soft. A dental t makes it paaththu, look. Keep paadunga.

wrong.label: English t and oo: paa-too
wrong.how: Say it like the English word: tongue tip on the ridge with a puff of air, no hold on the double, and a long English oo: PAA-too PAA-doon-ga.

phrases.ask: Ask for some water.
phrases.good: KON-jam THAN-Ni ku-dun-ga. The th of thaNNi is dental: tongue tip pressed on the back of your top teeth, no puff. It is NOT the th in 'thin'. ண்ண: curl the tip back, touch the roof and hold.

wrong.label: English th as in 'thin': θanni
wrong.how: Read the romanization the English way: th as in thin, with your tongue between your teeth and air hissing through: THIN-ni.

wrong.label: flat n, no hold: thani
wrong.how: Keep the dental th, but make the ண்ண a single quick English n with the tip on the ridge: THA-ni.

phrases.ask: Welcome a guest in and seat them.
phrases.good: VAAN-ga, uk-KAA-run-ga. Hold every aa about twice as long as feels natural, as in father. The r is a light everyday tap, the tongue tip just touching once. Even rhythm, no big stress.

wrong.label: every long vowel short: vunga, ukkarunga
wrong.how: Clip every vowel short, like the u in cup: VUN-ga, uk-KA-run-ga. Same consonants.

wrong.label: English r and English stress
wrong.how: Use an American r (tongue bunched, touching nothing) and hit the middle syllable hard, the English way: uk-KAAR-un-ga.

phrases.ask: Suggest watching a film tonight.
phrases.good: PA-dam paak-ka-LAA-maa? The first pa is SHORT, like the u in cup. Then hold paa, laa and maa long, and let the final maa rise as a question.

wrong.label: first vowel long: paadam (lesson)
wrong.how: Stretch the first syllable: PAA-dam. Everything else the same.

wrong.label: statement intonation, no question
wrong.how: Say it right, but flat and falling at the end, like announcing it, so the maa loses its rise.

phrases.ask: Tell me your leg hurts after the walk.
phrases.good: KAAL va-lik-ku-dhu. Hold kaal long. The doubled kk: stop for a beat before releasing. dhu: soft and dental.

wrong.label: short vowel: kal (stone)
wrong.how: Clip it: KAL, with the a like the u in cup.

wrong.label: doubled kk collapsed: valikudhu
wrong.how: Run va-li-ku-dhu together with a single quick k and no stop.

phrases.ask: Tell her the food is really good.
phrases.good: ROM-ba nal-LAA-ruk-ku, fused into one breath. Hold the doubled ll: start the l and stay on it a beat, then a long laa running straight into rukku.

wrong.label: single l, short a: nalarukku
wrong.how: Rush it: na-la-ruk-ku, with a single quick l and a short la.

wrong.label: unfused, word by word: nallaa irukku
wrong.how: Pull the words apart like a dictionary: ROM-ba. NAL-laa. I-RUK-ku. Three separate words with a small gap between each.

phrases.ask: Tell me you all went yesterday.
phrases.good: NAAN-ga NETH-thu po-NOAM. naa long. The th-th of neththu is dental and held. The ending is a long, pure oh (as in home, without the w glide), then close your lips on the m.

wrong.label: ending swallowed: ponum
wrong.how: Reduce the ending the English way: po-num, a lazy uh and a half-said m.

wrong.label: English th as in 'thin': neθu
wrong.how: Read neththu the English way: th as in thin, tongue between the teeth, no hold.

phrases.ask: Ask if that's enough rice.
phrases.good: POH-dhu-MAA? dh: tongue tip soft on the back of your top teeth. Then a long, rising maa that makes it a question.

wrong.label: question dropped: podhum
wrong.how: Clip the maa off entirely: POH-dhum. It stops being a question.

wrong.label: English d: podumaa
wrong.how: Use a hard English d, with the tip on the ridge behind the teeth instead of on the teeth: POH-du-maa.

phrases.ask: Your cousin looks upset. Ask what happened.
phrases.good: en-NAA-chu? Fused into one word, as the charter says fast speech does: the two words melt and the aa holds.

wrong.label: unfused: enna aachu
wrong.how: Say the two dictionary words separately: EN-na. AA-chu.

wrong.label: book form: enna aayitru
wrong.how: Say the written form: en-na aa-yit-ru.

phrases.ask: Tell me you're heading off now.
phrases.good: se-ri, POH-reen. Both r sounds are the same light tap: Coimbatore speakers mostly make no difference between ர and ற, so nothing is trilled. Hold the reen long.

wrong.label: book form: pogiren
wrong.how: Say the dictionary verb: se-ri, po-gi-ren.

wrong.label: hard trilled ற, the 'uncanny' over-articulation
wrong.how: Do what the TTS does: roll the r of poren hard, two or three flicks, and make it clearly harder than the r in seri.

phrases.ask: Tell me you forgot.
phrases.good: ma-RAN-dhut-teen. The ற is an ordinary light tap, the same as any r (her ruling: natives do not trill it). The doubled tt: curl the tip back and hold. Long teen.

wrong.label: hard trilled ற, the 'uncanny' over-articulation
wrong.how: Roll the ற hard, two or three flicks, the way the TTS voice does. Keep the rest right.

wrong.label: single t and short ending: marandhuten
wrong.how: Collapse the tt to one quick English t and clip the end: ma-ran-dhu-ten.

phrases.ask: Ask your mother-in-law if she has eaten.
phrases.good: saap-TEEN-ga-LAA? The spoken, contracted form: the pp barely stops, then a long tee and a long rising laa. This is the family's hello.

wrong.label: book form: saappitteergalaa
wrong.how: Spell it out in full, formal and slow: saap-pit-teer-ga-laa.

wrong.label: falling English question
wrong.how: Say the right words, but with the English yes/no tune, pitch dropping at the end instead of a held, rising laa.

phrases.ask: Tell the auto driver to stop here.
phrases.good: IN-ga ni-ruth-THUN-ga. The ற is a light tap, like any r. The th-th: tongue tip pressed on the back of the top teeth and held for the double.

wrong.label: hard trilled ற, the 'uncanny' over-articulation
wrong.how: Roll the r of niRu hard, the TTS way. Keep the rest right.

wrong.label: English th as in 'thin': niruθunga
wrong.how: Read the th the English way: tongue between the teeth, air hissing, no hold.

phrases.say: Office-ல work ரொம்ப heavy, அதான் late-ஆ வரேன்.
phrases.roman: Office-la work romba heavy, adhaan late-aa varen.
phrases.en: work at the office is really heavy, that's why I'm coming late
phrases.ask: Why are you late tonight?
phrases.good: Say it the way you'd actually say it to Anna: English words in your normal accent, Tamil words your best, all in one breath.

phrases.say: Weekend-ல family-ஓட beach-க்கு போனோம், super-ஆ இருந்துச்சு.
phrases.roman: Weekend-la family-oda beach-ku ponom, super-aa irundhuchu.
phrases.en: we went to the beach with the family at the weekend, it was great
phrases.ask: What did you do at the weekend?
phrases.good: Say it the way you'd actually say it to Anna: English words in your normal accent, Tamil words your best, all in one breath.

phrases.say: Sorry, எனக்கு புரியல, கொஞ்சம் slow-ஆ சொல்லுங்க.
phrases.roman: Sorry, enakku puriyala, konjam slow-aa sollunga.
phrases.en: sorry, I didn't understand, say it a bit slower
phrases.ask: (Anna just said something fast that he missed.)
phrases.good: Say it the way you'd actually say it to Anna: English words in your normal accent, Tamil words your best, all in one breath.

phrases.ask: What did you do today?
phrases.good: Anna asks; answer however you like, in any mix of Tamil and English. Then type what you meant.

phrases.en: have you eaten? what did you eat?
phrases.ask: Have you eaten? What did you eat?
phrases.good: Anna asks; answer however you like, in any mix of Tamil and English. Then type what you meant.

phrases.en: what did you like most in Coimbatore?
phrases.ask: What did you like most in Coimbatore?
phrases.good: Anna asks; answer however you like, in any mix of Tamil and English. Then type what you meant.
